paper.title: MDTeamGPT: A Self-Evolving LLM-based Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Disciplinary Team Medical Consultation
paper.central_claim: MDTeamGPT: a self-evolving multi-agent medical consultation framework (primary-care triage, specialist agents, lead-physician consensus aggregation with residual discussion, plus CorrectKB and ChainKB accumulating correct cases and error-reflection summaries) reaches 90.1% on MedQA and 83.9% on PubMedQA with gpt-4-turbo, and its knowledge bases generalize across datasets.

evidence.quote: The conclusion is later validated against the correct result.
evidence.support_explanation: KB routing uses the ground-truth answer: correct consultations go to CorrectKB, incorrect ones (with the correct answer and error reflection) to ChainKB; this privileged label exists only for benchmark-style training streams.

evidence.quote: Conversely, if the consultation outcome is incorrect
evidence.support_explanation: ChainKB record = initial hypothesis, analysis process, final conclusion, error reflection (+ correct answer) generated by a CoT Reviewer agent.

evidence.quote: these two knowledge bases are not referenced during the initial discussion round
evidence.support_explanation: Read path: top-K (K=5) cosine retrieval with text-embedding-3-small from both KBs, injected from round 2 (when conflicts arise) to keep first-round independence; no write-time dedup, forgetting or versioning described.

evidence.quote: containing only experiences from the training sets.
evidence.support_explanation: Construction/test separation stated: CorrectKB and ChainKB contain only training-set experiences; test sets of MedQA and PubMedQA are used for the reported results. Test-set sizes are not given.

evidence.quote: Ablation study evaluating the impact of different module compositions on accuracy metrics.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2 (MedQA/PubMedQA/avg): joint discussion 78.5/74.0/76.3; +residual 76.9/74.8/75.9; +lead 78.2/75.4/76.8; residual+lead 84.3/77.6/81.0; +CorrectKB only 87.3/83.5/85.4; +ChainKB only 85.2/78.1/81.6; full 90.1/83.9/87.0. Store-off vs full: +5.8 and +6.3 points.

Table 3: MedQA test with PubMedQA-built KBs 87.9 vs 84.3 no-KB (+3.6, in-domain KB 90.1); PubMedQA test with MedQA-built KBs 79.7 vs 77.6 (+2.1, in-domain KB 83.9). Most in-domain gain disappears across datasets.

evidence.quote: Main results on accuracy and F1-score across MedQA and PubMedQA datasets (all results were obtained using gpt-4-turbo).
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1: MDTeamGPT 90.1/83.9 (avg 87.0) vs Medprompt 90.2/82.0 (avg 86.1), Multi-expert 86.6/82.7, MedAgents 83.7/76.8, Single-agent 77.4/75.3; no seeds, intervals or test sizes.

evidence.quote: Although our approach achieves slightly lower accuracy on the MedQA dataset than Medprompt
evidence.support_explanation: Medprompt is attributed to four-option-only evaluation, i.e., the baseline protocol differs from the 4/5-option MedQA used here; comparison fairness unresolved.

evidence.quote: This benchmark was chosen after considering both performance and cost.
evidence.support_explanation: 600 consultation rounds per dataset are chosen with reference to performance, while Figure 4 plots test accuracy against rounds; selection partly informed by test curves.

evidence.quote: accuracy improves with more consultation samples and stabilizes after approximately 600 cases
evidence.support_explanation: Accuracy-vs-stored-cases curves for 7 LLMs show accumulation gains saturating near 600; values only in figures.

evidence.quote: resulting in a total of 10 test questions
evidence.support_explanation: Human evaluation uses 5 volunteers and 10 questions (ratings of accuracy, explainability, etc.); anecdotal. Efficiency rated low.

evidence.quote: primarily due to the increased time required for multi-round discussions among multiple roles compared to the Single-Agent approach
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede that efficiency is worse than a single agent, while the Introduction motivates the lead physician/residual structure as reducing cognitive load and improving efficiency; no token/latency numbers.

evidence.quote: If votes are evenly distributed, the final answer is randomly selected from the agents
evidence.support_explanation: Random tie-break and temperature 0.7 introduce run-to-run variance not reported.

gap.author_gap: Multi-role MDT dialogues grow long and burden the model; prior systems store histories without abstraction or error reflection, limiting generalization and self-evolution.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and addressed by KB ablation, but the nearest experience-based neighbors (ExpeL, IER, Agent Hospital, Co-Learning) are described, not run, so the claim that they cannot exploit errors is untested here.
lineage: MedAgents / multi-expert prompting / LLM Discussion (static multi-role) -> ExpeL / IER / Agent Hospital (experience stores) -> MDTeamGPT (correct/incorrect dual KB with error reflection + lead-physician residual structure)
gap.closest_adjacent: ExpeL, Agent Hospital, IER as characterized in Related Work; originals not in pinned package; Medprompt/MedAgents run as baselines in Table 1
gap.residue: Long multi-agent context; failing to reuse mistakes.
gap.remaining_gap: Gold-label-free deployment, KB growth and contamination, comparison with other experience stores, efficiency.
unresolved: Contamination of MedQA test with gpt-4-turbo pretraining or KB near-duplicates

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With gpt-4-turbo and gold-label-gated knowledge bases built from the training sets, retrieved correct-case and error-reflection records raise held-out accuracy by about 6 points on MedQA and PubMedQA (author-reported, single run); cross-dataset gains are about 2-4 points. Not shown: label-free deployment, contamination-free, budget-matched, or variance-controlled.

G.reason: Concrete limitations (context overload, no error-reflection stores) with named neighbors, but the neighbors that matter (ExpeL, Agent Hospital, IER) are not run and the residual after the method is only partly bounded.

M.reason: Dual KB (success summary vs error reflection with correct answer) and round-2 retrieval to keep independence are reasoned and the KB variants show differential effects, yet the claim that abstract reasoning rather than similar-case lookup transfers is asserted, and alternatives are not distinguished.

X.reason: Algorithms 1-2, prompts and record formats make the build/read chain reconstructable (gold-gated routing, top-5 cosine, read timing, round caps); maintenance (dedup, forgetting, staleness), failure handling and scale beyond 600 rounds are not specified.

E.measurement.reason: Accuracy and F1 against benchmark gold answers are reliable validators on standard datasets; deductions for undisclosed test sizes, random tie-breaks, and a Medprompt comparison under a different option protocol.

E.causality.reason: Clean KB-on/off and per-KB ablations plus module ablations, but no cheaper conditioning control (nearest-neighbor few-shot, same cases without reflection), no compute match with single-agent baselines, single run.

E.holdout.reason: Training-only KBs and a cross-dataset test are real separation; weaknesses: privileged gold labels in KB construction, no contamination/near-duplicate audit, 600-round point chosen with test curves visible, two datasets in one domain.

E.statistics.reason: Negative component results are reported (residual alone lowers accuracy) but no test sizes, seeds, intervals or repeats despite temperature 0.7 and random tie-breaking; interpreted deltas of 0.3-0.8 points are untested.

E.cost.reason: No tokens, calls, latency or build cost for multi-round multi-agent consultation plus 600-round KB construction; only a qualitative human remark that efficiency is lower.
